title: SAE dark matter
description: Sparse-autoencoder reconstruction errors contain predictable structure.

coverage.scope_note: This snapshot contains the saved merged final records used by this entry, including records not individually shown on the page. It is not an exhaustive collection of experiments or papers. Missing records, omitted extraction and not-tested statements are different from negative results.
coverage.source_check_note: Source checks are partial and sampled. A missing check means no returned check is in this snapshot; it does not establish that one was requested. Corrections and disagreements are reported separately and are not silently applied to the saved rows or classifications.

claims.heading: A substantial share of sparse autoencoder (SAE) error is linearly predictable from input activations
SAE errors are predictable across widths, with some components persisting
SAE reconstruction errors can be more harmful than equally large random errors
Linear SAE error may contain missed features; nonlinear error may resist learning feature sets
SAE feature analyses can fail to preserve model behavior when error terms are omitted
Unexplained SAE reconstruction error mostly reflects training artifacts

related_findings.title: Reconstruction depends on SAE design and optimization
related_findings.summary: The encoder's flexibility, the directions of learned features, constraints on sparse outputs and optimization all affect reconstruction error. Their relative importance varies across settings.

examples.headline: iSAE-ME sharply reduces reconstruction error on noiseless sparse-linear synthetic data.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Reconstruction error varies across inputs
related_findings.summary: Reconstruction error varies across token types, positions, contexts, languages and formatting. Aggregate fidelity can hide these differences, and larger error need not imply poorer model capability.

examples.headline: Reconstruction quality and downstream cross-entropy changes worsen beyond the SAE's training context, especially in early layers.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Fidelity varies across layers and activation sites
related_findings.summary: Reconstruction accuracy and the cost to model behavior of replacing activations depend on the layer, the role of the activations and the decomposition method. There is no universal trend with depth.

examples.headline: Yi-6B layer-30 Values reconstruct less faithfully than Keys at K=8; increasing K improves Value fidelity.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Transfer depends on compatible representations
related_findings.summary: Transferring an SAE across layers, seeds, checkpoints and fine-tuning stages depends on how well their representations match. Aligning representations or training on the target representations can improve otherwise unsuccessful transfer.

examples.headline: A fixed CLIP SAE transfers poorly after standard fine-tuning; L2 regularization or SAE-FT improves fidelity.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Activation fidelity does not guarantee preserved behavior
related_findings.summary: Activation reconstruction metrics do not reliably predict whether loss, task performance or steering effectiveness will be preserved. Some poorly reconstructed directions have little importance for model behavior.

examples.headline: π0.5 mean-pool SAEs preserve activation fidelity but sharply reduce success, without matched random-error controls.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Feature interventions depend on the setting
related_findings.summary: SAE features can support causal interventions and steering. Their effectiveness depends on behavior, seed, sparsity and intervention design, and need not exceed simple dense baselines.

examples.headline: Amplifying the top-10 SAE feature activations from PatchTST's feedforward network by 5× shifts forecasts.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Reconstruction can preserve measured task performance
related_findings.summary: Replacing activations with SAE reconstructions can preserve measured task performance in selected models, activation sites and SAE configurations.

examples.headline: Phi-3 Mini layer-6 Top-k reconstruction slightly lowers MMLU scores while improving TruthfulQA and GSM8k scores.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Information preservation depends on the task
related_findings.summary: Sparse codes and reconstructions retain some information that linear models can read, while losing information needed for other tasks. Comparing probes alone does not explain how reconstruction error carries information.

examples.headline: Reconstructed vectors underperform dense vectors on held-out cross-architecture retrieval at both tested anchor settings.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Host representations affect reconstruction difficulty
related_findings.summary: Reconstruction difficulty depends on the host representation's geometry, architecture and training, as well as the SAE.

examples.headline: At matched feature capacity and sparsity, MoWE feedforward updates reconstruct more accurately than dense feedforward updates.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Specialization and expansion recover some missing features
related_findings.summary: Domain specialization, dictionaries trained on reconstruction errors and dictionary expansion can recover features an SAE misses. These results do not separate reconstruction error that follows linear relationships from error that does not.

examples.headline: Transferring novel features from GPT2-1536 into GPT2-768 lowers the smaller SAE's reconstruction error.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Wider dictionaries can leave residual error
related_findings.summary: Wider dictionaries reduce aggregate reconstruction error or replacement loss in some settings, while error remains over the tested range. This does not establish an asymptotic floor or shared failures across tokens.

examples.headline: Increasing SAE expansion reduces mean squared reconstruction error at a DDPM++ U-Net bottleneck trained on CelebA-HQ.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Sparsity affects reconstruction and downstream fidelity
related_findings.summary: The number of active features allowed and the sparsity penalty can govern reconstruction accuracy and the cost to downstream model behavior. Improvements sometimes require codes with more active features.

examples.headline: Larger k improves SMI-TED fidelity; dictionary expansion minimally affects changes in loss at matched sparsity.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Reconstruction can impair downstream performance
related_findings.summary: Replacing activations with SAE reconstructions can worsen downstream loss or task performance. These comparisons alone do not establish excess harm relative to matched random errors.

examples.headline: GPT-2 Small layer-8 reconstruction raises OpenWebText perplexity, without a random-error comparison.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Restoring error can help or hurt
related_findings.summary: Removing reconstruction error or selected components can improve loss or intervention scores. The benefit of retaining error depends on the objective and configuration.

examples.headline: Restoring ScopeSAE error perpendicular to the gradient raises cross-entropy; restoring the parallel component lowers cross-entropy.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Fidelity and interpretability can diverge
related_findings.summary: Better reconstruction or downstream loss does not guarantee more faithful or interpretable features. Feature interpretability also need not track causal importance.

examples.headline: Combining toy-model features gives lower reconstruction error than keeping only some of the correct features.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Perturbation comparisons depend on direction and geometry
related_findings.summary: Perturbations with equal norms can have different behavioral effects. Comparisons also depend on how random baselines account for activation geometry.

examples.headline: OpenVLA steering along decoder vectors harms success more than equal-magnitude random steering; reconstruction was not tested.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Token identity and frequency shape error
related_findings.summary: Token frequency and identity explain some reconstruction error, and token-specific biases can absorb part of it. The SAE reduces feature activation strengths by different amounts depending on how often and strongly features activate.

examples.headline: A token-specific decoder bias reduces added cross-entropy across the tested Pythia-1.4B layers.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Wider dictionaries do not always improve reconstruction
related_findings.summary: Increasing dictionary width alone need not improve reconstruction when the active-feature budget or sparsity penalty is fixed. Worsening reconstruction can coincide with more features that never activate.

examples.headline: On PTB-XL at fixed k, wider dictionaries lower validation R² overall and increase dead features.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Fewer features that never activate need not improve fidelity
related_findings.summary: Reducing the number of features that never activate, or preventing feature activation strengths from being reduced, does not by itself guarantee lower reconstruction error or downstream loss.

examples.headline: On SONNY, B-spline curves replace ReLU, reducing features that never activate but capturing less activation variance.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Adaptation and training choices change replacement cost
related_findings.summary: Adaptation, training objectives and sparsity implementations can change the functional cost of SAE reconstruction. Gains depend on the model and configuration.

examples.headline: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) reduces cross-entropy when multiple Llama Scope SAEs jointly replace activations.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Replacement errors accumulate across layers
related_findings.summary: Repeated SAE replacement accumulates reconstruction-induced error across layers. The accumulation depends on training method and how cross-layer inputs are represented.

examples.headline: Inserting 5 SAEs together raises cross-entropy to almost 10 nats, units based on natural logarithms.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Error magnitude and components can be predicted
related_findings.summary: Activations or sparse features can predict the size of SAE reconstruction errors and some components of those errors. Predicting an error's size and predicting its full direction and size are distinct tasks.

examples.headline: Activations linearly predict substantial variation in squared error magnitude, less in early and final layers.
A model predicts reconstruction errors from SAE feature activations, with its linear term providing most improvement.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Low-rank components can carry important information
related_findings.summary: Low-rank channels can capture causally important information or correct part of reconstruction-induced loss. Learned scaffolds and corrective adapters are different objects.

examples.headline: Removing a learned 24-dimensional component raises cross-entropy more than removing the top-24 principal components.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Error-related information can act through different routes
related_findings.summary: Information associated with reconstruction error can affect behavior through downstream SAE features or perturbations in directions the SAE does not capture. The evidence does not establish a common process linking this information to behavior across these settings.

examples.headline: Under a Gemma-2B refusal clamp, SAE-unexplained recovery perturbations restore non-refusal more often than SAE-feature changes.

reading_list.why: Introduces the original split into linear and nonlinear error, error prediction and scaling results, with code and controls.
Independently tests separation of linear and nonlinear error in medical-domain SAEs and examines specialization; controls and uncertainty are unreported.
Compares reconstruction errors with equally large random errors and tests shrinkage, revealing differences across locations in the model.

known_gaps.summary: Independent support, source accuracy, missing evidence and experimental coverage remain uncertain, limiting how broadly the findings can be generalized.
items: Independent authorship and shared experiments have not been checked across studies grouped under the same theme. Apparent agreement may therefore overstate independent support.
Some potentially relevant studies remain unevaluated or lack available source text. Their effect on the conclusions is unknown.
The available evidence lacks detailed measurements for some GPT scaling and clinical expansion results, limiting assessment of those findings.
Evidence coverage across model families and sizes remains uncertain. Model size or training stage is sometimes unspecified, limiting conclusions about generality.
Source checks found factual errors, and it remains unclear whether all affected conclusions were corrected.
Some combined findings still need verification against each study's experimental conditions. A citation alone does not establish that a broader conclusion preserves those conditions.
